title: 377. Geometry, Spatial Thinking & Measurement: Distance from a Point to a Line
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Distance from the origin to a line
questions.question: What is the perpendicular distance from \((0,0)\) to \(3x+4y-12=0\)?
questions.hint: Divide the absolute substitution result by the coefficient-vector length.

questions.learningObjective: Substitute a point into the normalized distance formula.
questions.question: What is the perpendicular distance from \((1,1)\) to \(3x+4y-12=0\)?
questions.explanation: The numerator is \(\lvert3+4-12\rvert=5\), and the denominator is \(5\). The distance is \(1\).
questions.hint: Evaluate the numerator using both point coordinates.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a horizontal gap to a vertical line.
questions.question: What is the perpendicular distance from \((5,-2)\) to \(x=1\)?
questions.explanation: The shortest segment is horizontal, with length \(\lvert5-1\rvert=4\).
questions.hint: A vertical line fixes the horizontal coordinate.

questions.learningObjective: Calculate a vertical gap to a horizontal line.
questions.question: What is the perpendicular distance from \((3,4)\) to \(y=-1\)?
questions.explanation: The shortest segment is vertical, with length \(\lvert4-(-1)\rvert=5\).
questions.hint: Compare the point's vertical coordinate with the line's fixed value.

questions.learningObjective: Compute an exact radical point-to-line distance.
questions.question: What is the perpendicular distance from \((2,-1)\) to \(2x-y+3=0\)?
questions.explanation: The numerator is \(\lvert4+1+3\rvert=8\). The denominator is \(\sqrt{2^2+(-1)^2}=\sqrt{5}\), giving \(\frac{8}{\sqrt{5}}\).
questions.hint: Use the Euclidean length of the two coefficients in the denominator.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize zero distance when a point satisfies a line equation.
questions.question: What is the perpendicular distance from \((1,2)\) to \(2x+y-4=0\)?
questions.explanation: Substitution gives \(2(1)+2-4=0\). The point lies on the line, so its distance is \(0\).
questions.hint: Test whether the point already belongs to the line.

questions.learningObjective: Check that equivalent line equations give the same distance.
questions.question: The equations \(6x+8y-20=0\) and \(3x+4y-10=0\) describe the same line. What is its distance from the origin?
questions.explanation: Using the first equation gives \(\frac{20}{\sqrt{36+64}}=2\). Using the second gives \(\frac{10}{5}=2\), confirming invariance.
questions.hint: Scale the numerator and denominator consistently.

questions.concept: Line constant from a given distance
questions.learningObjective: Recover a positive constant in a line equation.
questions.question: The line \(5x+12y+c=0\) is at distance \(3\) from the origin, and \(c>0\). What is \(c\)?
questions.explanation: The distance is \(\frac{\lvert c\rvert}{13}\). Thus \(c=3\cdot13=39\), using the positive condition.
questions.hint: Write the origin-to-line distance in terms of the unknown constant.

questions.learningObjective: Compare center-to-line distance with a circle's radius.
questions.question: A circle has center \((-1,2)\) and radius \(3\). How does the line \(3x+4y-20=0\) meet the circle?

options.label: A
options.text: It cuts the circle at two distinct points.

options.label: B
options.text: It is tangent to the circle.

questions.explanation: The center's distance to the line is \(\frac{\lvert-3+8-20\rvert}{5}=3\), equal to the radius. Equality gives tangency.
questions.hint: Compare the perpendicular center-to-line distance with the radius.

questions.concept: Point parameter from a line distance
questions.learningObjective: Solve an absolute-value distance equation with a positivity condition.
questions.question: A point \((k,k)\), with \(k>0\), is at perpendicular distance \(\sqrt{2}\) from \(x+y-2=0\). What is \(k\)?
questions.explanation: The equation is \(\frac{\lvert2k-2\rvert}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}\), so \(\lvert2k-2\rvert=2\). Its solutions are \(0\) and \(2\); positivity selects \(2\).
questions.hint: Keep both absolute-value cases until applying the sign condition.
